north_star.label: Inference from docs
north_star.value: Build a deterministic long-only daily-bar regime-filtered trend/relative-strength pullback breakout engine that buys strong names resting in strong markets and can progress through research, paper, shadow, and audit review with repeatable evidence.

purpose.label: Fact plus inference
purpose.value: Python package implementing the strategy core, local paper/shadow runtime, persistence, backtesting, analytics, and audit reporting for the RF_TPC_V2 swing trading system.

strengths: Strong deterministic v2.1 strategy specification and config.
Core strategy formulas and state invariants are represented directly in code.
Good unit-test breadth for a prototype, now including replay workflow, immutable comparison snapshot coverage, immutable audit snapshot coverage, and PASS/WARN/FAIL review scenario coverage.
Paper/shadow/audit layer gives a useful bridge before live trading.

Pydantic contracts, prepared-data validators, SQLAlchemy state models, Alembic migrations, artifact plus per-intent runtime event history, immutable comparison snapshots, immutable audit snapshots with snapshot_id/snapshot_batch_id/recorded_at review output, OperatorReviewReport, threshold-driven review checks, structured review-run metrics, repeated review trend summaries, JSON/HTML threshold-breach checks, operator response guidance, and static HTML rendering make domain boundaries explicit.
weaknesses: Broker execution is paper-only; no live broker adapter is present.
No ingestion, feature store, reference master, corporate action service, earnings feed, or broker position service.

README, examples, local paper/shadow/audit workflow, run history, event ledger, Alembic migrations, local runbook, environment template, and CI exist; scheduler, deployment, and production runbooks remain absent.
Migrations exist, but runtime still uses create_all locally and there is no production migration/rollback runbook.
Ruff lint and the seven-file typed-core mypy gate pass; strict full-package mypy still fails with known errors.

Observability is limited to in-process alert objects, report files, runtime events, structured local review metrics, and local JSON/YAML/HTML review artifacts; there is no external logging, alerting, or live dashboard stack.

risks.risk: Accidental overestimation of live readiness because paper/shadow CLI exists but live data, broker, deployment, and operations are absent.
Incorrect or non-point-in-time input data can invalidate signals because ingestion and data validation are out of repo scope.
Config fields imply unimplemented controls, including rate-limit guard, PBO, and some backtest realism flags.
Paper-shadow audit snapshots preserve review output, but each new audit batch is still generated from latest paper/broker/shadow state at review time.

unknowns: Live data vendor and point-in-time guarantees.
Chosen live broker, API credentials, permissions, order semantics, and sandbox path.
Production deployment target, scheduler, secret store, and alerting stack.
Business risk limits and KPI thresholds for launch.
Whether a separate orchestrator/agent repo is expected to operate this package.

recommendations.recommendation: Promote the tiny manifest-backed replay proof into a general historical replay runner with run-scoped artifacts, while keeping validator preconditions and excluding performance baselining.
Enforce the roadmap process before more feature work: design grouped delivery batches, state non-goals, group implementation/tests/docs, and record validation.
Extend from the general replay runner to larger manifest-backed historical panels after deterministic replay artifacts are stable.
Expand typed-core coverage at reporting and audit boundaries.
